title: Topic 38 | Average speeds of gas molecules

questions.text: By what factor must the absolute temperature of an ideal gas be raised for the root-mean-square speed of its molecules to double?
How many times smaller is the root-mean-square speed of thermal motion of an oxygen molecule than that of a hydrogen molecule?
How does the root-mean-square speed of nitrogen molecules change if the absolute temperature of the gas increases 4 times?
By what factor does the root-mean-square speed of ideal gas molecules decrease when its absolute temperature decreases 2 times?
If the temperature of a gas increases by 21%, by what percentage does the root-mean-square speed of its molecules increase?
At what temperature (K) is the root-mean-square speed of nitrogen molecules 830 m/s? MNitrogen = 28 g/mol.
Find the root-mean-square speed of hydrogen molecules at 27°C (km/s) and the momentum of one molecule moving at this speed (kg · m/s). The molar mass of hydrogen is µ = 2.0 g/mol.

Treating air as a homogeneous gas, find how many times smaller the root-mean-square speed of a dust particle of mass 1.74 · 10⁻¹² kg suspended in air is than the root-mean-square speed of air molecules. Mair = 29 g/mol.
By what factor does the root-mean-square speed of ideal gas molecules increase when its absolute temperature increases 3 times?
Molecules of which gas in the atmosphere move fastest?
The temperature of a gas rose from 10°C to 20°C. How does the root-mean-square speed of thermal motion of its molecules change?
At what temperature (K) is the root-mean-square speed of hydrogen molecules 2 km/s? The molar mass of hydrogen is 0.002 kg/mol.
To what temperature must a gas in a sealed vessel be heated from 250°C for the root-mean-square speed of its molecules to double?

When the root-mean-square speed of gas molecules increased from 600 m/s to 750 m/s, the temperature rose by 30 K. By how much will the temperature rise (K) if the root-mean-square speed increases from 750 m/s to 900 m/s?

When the root-mean-square speed of gas molecules increased from 500 m/s to 620 m/s, the temperature rose by 70 K. By how much will the temperature rise (K) if the root-mean-square speed increases from 620 m/s to 800 m/s?
Calculate the root-mean-square speed (m/s) and the translational kinetic energy (J) of hydrogen molecules at a temperature of 173 K. MH = 2 g/mol.
Calculate the average translational kinetic energy of one gas molecule at standard conditions (J).
Calculate the root-mean-square speed (m/s) and the translational kinetic energy (J) of hydrogen molecules at a temperature of 273 K. MH = 2 g/mol.
In Stern's experiment, the silver strip (track) that appears on the inner surface of the outer cylinder turns out to be smeared. What conclusion can be drawn from this?
answers: The speeds of the molecules are different
The speeds of the molecules are the same
It does not depend on the speeds of the molecules

questions.text: In Stern's experiment, if the rotation frequency of the apparatus is 150 s⁻¹ and the angular displacement of a silver molecule is 5.4°, what speed did the silver vapor molecule have (m/s)? The distance between the inner and outer cylinders is 2 cm.
